title: Econ Lab: Catalyst Field Protocol for Batched Inference & KV Prefetching
creator: Priya Patel
description: Purpose: establish a reusable field protocol (experiment catalog + runbook) that lets product and econ-ops rapidly evaluate combined batching, KV-prefetch, and mixed quantization strategies against production traffic slices. Scope: create 6 experiment templates (3 batching profiles x 2 prefetch heuristics), telemetry schema, guardrail thresholds, launch checklist, and a small analysis workbook. Out of scope: model architecture changes and wholesale kernel rewrites. Why now: multiple customer signals indicate latency-sensitive workloads are still cost-prohibitive; prior lab work found ~18-28% token-cost savings under synthetic workloads but lacked production-grade validation and regression guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 6 experiment templates committed to repo and visible in Console; 2) Telemetry schema (cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, quality regression signals) deployed to prod tracing; 3) Safety guardrails defined and automated in the rollout (auto-revert triggers for >3% quality regression or >15% latency increase on target slice); 4) Field run completed on two customer-similar slices and results summarized in the Econ Lab workbook; 5) Post-mortem with decisions and next actions published to Confluence.
tasks: Draft experiment templates (batch sizes, batching window, kv-prefetch TTLs)
Implement telemetry hooks: token_cost, token_count, latency_p50_p95, quality_regression_score
Create rollout runbook with rollback triggers
Ship Console view for active experiments and per-slice metrics
Coordinate with Sales/CS to identify two low-risk customer slices for field runs
Run pilot cluster experiments on Dedicated nodes and capture traces
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting — aligned PM, Eng, and Observability. Agreed experiment templates and telemetry fields. Owner assignments made.
2026-03-01: ENG spike completed (ENG-48210) — batcher changes validated in staging, observed 12% cost drop on synthetic bench with 5% p95 latency increase.
2026-03-04: Observability added quality_regression_score metric; initial thresholds proposed by Research (Priya).
2026-03-07: Integration test failed in heavy tail traffic — p95 latency regressed >20% with aggressive prefetch TTL. Task opened to add adaptive TTL (ENG-49721).
2026-03-10: Decided to proceed with conservative TTLs for first two field runs; expanded rollback conditions to include error rate spikes (>0.5% absolute).
risks: Key risks: 1) Quality regressions unnoticed by coarse metrics (mitigation: small canonical prompt set and automated A/B quality scoring); 2) Cross-slice signal contamination — run experiments on isolated tenant slices where possible; 3) Unexpected autoscaler interactions when batching reduces per-request throughput (mitigation: preflight load tests and temporary autoscale hold).
metrics: Primary: token_cost_savings (absolute and %), latency_p95, quality_regression_delta. Secondary: deploy_reverts, error_rate, customer_impact_events. Target: demonstrate >=15% median token cost savings on experimental slice with <3% quality regression and <10% p95 latency uplift.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (now-2w): templates + telemetry in staging. Phase 1 (2w-4w): pilot on internal traffic slices (canary customers). Phase 2 (4w-6w): two controlled customer slice field runs with Sales/CS coordination. Phase 3 (post 6w): retrospective and decision: scale to Dedicated or productize templates in Console. Auto-revert and alerting configured before Phase 1.
notes: Design trade-off: prefer conservative prefetch TTLs combined with smarter cache population heuristics to avoid tail latencies. Open question: whether to expose batch-window knob in Console or keep as an internal experiment parameter for initial rollout. Next sync scheduled 2026-03-15.
